title: Pedro Machado: From going concern to gone concern: The supervision-resolution continuum after a decade of the Single Resolution Mechanism
summary: I’m delighted to be taking part in this edition of the Bank Resolution Academy . Let me begin by thanking the Florence School of Banking and Finance for the invitation, and for their continued investment in something too easily taken for granted: building a community of practitioners with a common understanding of supervision and resolution. Today, I can offer you a point of view, shaped by my own particular experiences in this field. I spent five years at the Single Resolution Board, responsible for resolution planning and decision-making, and – since last year – I’ve served as a member of European banking supervision’s Supervisory Board.

title: Claudia Buch: Digital innovation: hindrance or booster for banks’ business models?
summary: Banking is, in essence, about processing information and making predictions – about the future liquidity needs of depositors, the ability of borrowers to repay loans, the quality of collateral. Some of the necessary information is measurable, while some is rather “soft” and comes from repeated interaction with customers. Traditionally, banks have had a key competitive advantage over other financial institutions: by providing different financial services under one roof, they obtain valuable information to make predictions. Digital innovation may thus change banks’ competitive advantages – it can hinder or boost their business models.

title: SRB statement on the tragic incident on its premises
summary: We are deeply saddened by the tragic gas incident that occurred at the Single Resolution Board's Treurenberg premises in Brussels on Friday afternoon, 14 August. All SRB staff had been safely evacuated from the building before the explosions occurred. Our thoughts are with everyone affected. We extend our sincere condolences to the family and colleagues of the firefighter who lost his life, and to those who were injured. The SRB remains in close contact with the Belgian authorities and emergency services as they continue to establish the circumstances surrounding the incident. We are grateful to the emergency services for their response and continued work.

MREL aims to ensure that a bank maintains sufficient loss-absorbing capacity to ensure that in resolution its shareholders and creditors would absorb the costs of any failure of the bank. title: The Single Resolution Board welcomes the European Commission's “Communication on the Competitiveness of the Banking Sector and the Single Market in Banking”
summary: From a crisis management perspective, the SRB appreciates the report's comprehensive approach, blending simplification with measures to foster market integration, from deposit insurance to liquidity in resolution. This aligns with the SRB view that competitiveness is best fostered not only by simpler, fewer rules, but also by completing the Banking Union to reap the benefits of a true Single Market. The SRB recommends to pursue the development of these first ideas while finding the right balance between flexibility and predictability.

title: Insurance products sold in Belgium: a new overview by the FSMA
summary: The FSMA has published ‘Insurance products in the spotlight’, an overview of the insurance products offered on the Belgian market. The document contains key figures about the insurance sector, such as the number of providers and the types of insurance contracts, and also shows developments over time. In addition, it gives clear insight into the way the premiums collected are allocated and the sometimes significant differences among insurers in that regard.

title: 25 new fraudulent platforms added to the FSMA’s list

These platforms lure investors online with promises of quick and easy earnings. summary: The European Central Bank (ECB) has published indicative operational calendars for 2028, which may affect financial institutions in their planning and compliance activities. This guidance is relevant to banks and other financial entities supervised by the ECB.

title: Christine Lagarde: Back to basics in an uncertain environment
summary: ECB President Christine Lagarde emphasizes a return to basics in an uncertain environment, which may impact financial institutions' risk management and compliance strategies. This guidance is relevant to various EU financial institutions, including banks and investment firms.
so_what: The speech by Christine Lagarde has informational value regarding the ECB's expectations on financial institutions' risk management and compliance in uncertain times.

title: Virtual outreach event on FSB sound practices for financial institutions’ responsible adoption of artificial intelligence
summary: On 7 July 2026 the FSB hosted a virtual event as part of the consultation process for its proposed sound practices for financial institutions’ responsible adoption of AI. On 10 June 2026, the Financial Stability Board published a consultation report on Sound Practices for Responsible Adoption of Artificial Intelligence (AI) to help financial institutions responsibly navigate AI adoption in a rapidly evolving technological landscape. As part of its consultation, the FSB hosted a virtual outreach event on Tuesday 7 July 2026. The event aimed to inform stakeholders about the consultation and to gather preliminary perspectives on the topics covered in the consultation report.

title: The FSMA publishes its 2025 annual report and outlines some pathways for third-pillar pensions
summary: The Financial Services and Markets Authority (FSMA) has published its 2025 annual report. The report describes how the FSMA has fulfilled its mission over the past year to contribute to a financial system that is worthy of its users’ trust. On the occasion of this publication, the FSMA also outlined some pathways for the reform and strengthening of third-pillar pensions.

title: EBA aligns Pillar 3 framework with EU green agenda - FinTech Global
summary: The European Banking Authority (EBA) has aligned its Pillar 3 framework with the EU's green agenda, which affects Banks and other financial institutions. This alignment aims to promote transparency and accountability in the financial sector's environmental impact.
so_what: The concrete compliance implication is that financial institutions will need to disclose their environmental, social, and governance (ESG) risks and impacts, which may require updates to their reporting and disclosure practices.
action: Review existing Pillar 3 reporting and disclosure practices to ensure alignment with the updated EBA framework

title: Crypto-assets service providers – End of the transitional period
summary: Crypto-asset service providers (CASP) must, as of 1 July 2026, hold an authorisation as a CASP. Without such authorisation, they must cease offering these services in Europe. The European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA) has already issued a statement on 17 April 2026 and reiterates its expectations by publishing the following communication on the matter.

title: ECB to integrate non-financial credit claim portfolios into general collateral framework, phasing out temporary measures
summary: The European Central Bank (ECB) will integrate non-financial credit claim portfolios into its general collateral framework, affecting banks and other financial institutions that use the ECB's collateral framework. This change will phase out temporary measures that were put in place.
so_what: The integration of non-financial credit claim portfolios into the general collateral framework may require adjustments to collateral management and risk assessment processes for affected institutions.
action: Review collateral management policies and procedures to ensure compliance with the updated general collateral framework

title: Isabel Schnabel: Interview with Die Zeit

title: Decision by the FSMA Sanctions Committee in the EXMAR NV case
summary: By a decision taken on 24 June 2026, the Sanctions Committee of the FSMA imposed an administrative fine of 350,000 euros on EXMAR NV for two infringements of Article 17 of the Market Abuse Regulation. The company had failed to publish as soon as possible the inside information that was available to it on 19 May 2020 and 18 June 2020.

title: ECB reports on progress towards euro adoption
summary: The European Central Bank (ECB) has reported on progress towards euro adoption, which may affect financial institutions in EU member states that have not yet adopted the euro. This development is relevant to various types of financial entities, including Banks and Investment Firms, operating in these countries.
so_what: The report has informational value regarding the ECB's efforts to support euro adoption, but it does not introduce new regulatory requirements for financial institutions.
